newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down from high prior close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down from high prior close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 95 basis points at 17.55 percent in early trade on Wednesday, from what traders said was an unrepresentatively high prior close.
Dealers said lower U.S. long bond yields could offset upside pressure on secondary rates expected due to month-end demand for liquidity.
"The (U.S.) long bond is more stable...so we don't see much pressure from that quarter, just from what could happen with the month closing," a trader said.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were meanwhile up 11/32 to yield 7.00 percent.
Traders said they did not expect a volatile session, but cautioned that secondary rates could rise in the wake of primary rate hikes.

"The market looks like being quiet all day, with little movement, and not even any month-end pressures, which may hit the market on Friday. Rates could adjust in line with the primary auction," another trader said.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 18.31 percent at Tuesday night's auction of government securities. This was a rise of 24 basis points since last week and compared with an average increase of 12 basis points predicted in a Reuters survey conducted prior to the auction.
Overnight rates on bank paper were down 40 basis points to 18.60 percent.
Liquidity of 1.653 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
